mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority of the holder's country of citizenship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the country of issuance

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registraire des entreprises du Québec; or Corporations Canada if a federal name reservation is used
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Not required for domestic public documents; no apostille or consular legalization required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners against FINTRAC politically exposed persons (PEP) criteria, including domestic PEPs, foreign PEPs, and heads of international organizations as defined under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations; mandatory screening against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, Canada's regulations under the Special Economic Measures Act, the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, the Canadian Departmental Sanctions List, and all domestic autonomous sanctions administered by Global Affairs Canada; where USD clearing or US counterparties are involved, supplemental screening against OFAC SDN and other OFAC sanctions lists is required. Client identification and verification must be completed before engagement, with enhanced due diligence and source-of-wealth confirmation applicable to the medium-risk vintage luxury consignment resale business model.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec - Online Services (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca/en/); federal alternative: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre (https://www.ic.gc.ca/app/scr/cc/CorporationsCanada) with NUANS name search report
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (C.Q.L.R. c. C-11) and its regulations, any corporate name used in Quebec must be in French or include a French version; the French version must be given at least equal prominence on public signage, business documents, and commercial communications. Names in a non-French language may be used as a version of the French name, but the French version remains mandatory for Quebec operations. All names must be expressed in Latin script; non-Latin names require certified transliteration or official romanization acceptable to the Registraire des entreprises. The name must be distinctive, not confusingly similar to existing names, not misleading, and not contrary to public order or morality.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registraire des entreprises rejects a proposed name, the applicant may file a written administrative review within 30 days of the refusal, setting out the legal and factual grounds for contesting the decision and proposing an alternative name. The administrative review is submitted through the Registraire's online services or by registered mail to the Registraire des entreprises. If the review is denied, the applicant may appeal to the Superior Court of Quebec within 30 days of the decision under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. For a federal name, a request for reconsideration may be made to the Director of Corporations Canada, and a refusal may be appealed to the Federal Court under section 23 of the Canada Business Corporations Act. In practice, where rejection rests on confusion or prohibited tokens, a revised name with a new NUANS name search report is filed before pursuing formal appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible as a registered service address in Quebec only if it provides a physical street address in Quebec, is not a post office box, and has a registered agent authorized to accept legal service. However, for an online vintage luxury resale business classified as Medium_Risk_Enhanced, a virtual office alone will not satisfy the commercial substance and AML/CFT expectations of Revenu Québec, banks, payment processors, or consignment counterparties. A physical business location, such as a secured warehouse, showroom, or boutique, should be maintained for inventory custody, authentication, and client-facing operations; a virtual office may be used only as an auxiliary administrative address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 25% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 12 months of operation by Revenu Québec or municipal licensing authorities, increasing to approximately 40% where the only registered office is a virtual address and the business maintains significant luxury consignment inventory. The quantified estimate reflects the elevated AML/CFT risk profile of secondhand luxury goods resale and the compliance burden associated with online payment rails such as Stripe and Escrow_Pay.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), CQLR c S-31.1, ss. 4, 8, 11-12 (articles of incorporation), 63 (registered office), 96-112 (board of directors, officers, and corporate governance)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (statuts de constitution) and certificate of constitution issued by REQ
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required under the QBCA; the authorized capital may be nominal (C$1 or as set in the articles). No statutory escrow account is required for paid-up capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) the articles of incorporation and registration of the Corporation under the Quebec Business Corporations Act are hereby confirmed; (2) the subscribed shares are allotted to the parties set out in the share subscription register for lawful consideration satisfactory to the board; (3) the registered office is established at the address appearing in the articles, within Quebec; (4) the individuals named on the directors consent list are elected first directors; (5) the officers listed in the officer register are appointed as President, Secretary and Treasurer; and (6) the directors are authorized to open a business bank account, issue share certificates and complete all filings with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec and tax authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name clearance and Nuans search request
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – online services.requebec.ssq.gouv.qc.ca
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed legal name to REQ together with a Nuans search request. Ensure the name complies with Quebec's Charter of the French Language branding rules and the corporate name requirements of QBCA. A French version or a clearly descriptive bilingual presentation is recommended for a Quebec-headquartered corporation.
required_dossiers: Identity and contact details of incorporators
Brief description of the business activity (ISIC 4791)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ flags a confusing or prohibited name, promptly file alternative names in priority order, obtain a letter of non-opposition from the conflicting name holder, or amend the proposed name in response to REQ's objections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and electronic filing of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – online corporate filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the QBCA statutory articles, setting out the corporation's name, share structure, share classes, restrictions on share transfers, first directors, and registered office. Execute the articles before a witness and file electronically with REQ together with the directors' consents and Nuans report. The corporation comes into existence upon issuance of the certificate of constitution.
required_dossiers: Consent of each director to act
Proof of registered office address in Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ returns a notice of irregularity, amend the articles and refile with a covering letter explaining the correction, using the same corporate name and Nuans report without restarting the name clearance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of certificate of constitution and Quebec enterprise number (NEQ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – corporate registry and certification service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the content of the certificate of constitution and the corresponding REQ enterprise register extract. Retain the enterprise number (NEQ) and use it for all interaction with Revenu Québec, municipal authorities, and commercial counterparties.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If there is an error in the published registry data, file a declaration of correction with REQ under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, and request a revised extract.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online; Revenu Québec – online business account registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for the federal Business Number (BN), GST/HST account, and Quebec Sales Tax (QST) account using the corporation's legal name, NEQ, and registered office. If the corporation will have employees, open the payroll deduction account in the same session. For an e-commerce resale platform, confirm the place of supply rules regarding digital goods and cross-province sales.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA or Revenu Québec rejects or queries the application, correct the consolidated business information by telephone with the Business Window or in writing with supporting constitutional documents, and promptly file a revised registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory registers, share subscription, and first board governance records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and corporate secretary; REQ for any registry updates
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the corporation's statutory registers at the registered office, record the issuance of subscribed shares to the original shareholders, and maintain the register of directors and officers. Adopt the first board resolution approving the share allotment, registered office, and officer appointments. Issue share certificates and file any change of directors or office address with REQ within the statutory timeline.
required_dossiers: Share subscription register and share certificates
Bylaw or unanimous shareholder agreement (if adopted)
Consent to act of each officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If corporate registers are found incomplete during an internal audit, call a directors' meeting, cure the omissions by written resolution, and file the corresponding declaration of change with REQ.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal and environmental compliance clearance for e-commerce operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal permit office (e.g., Ville de Montréal, Service des permis et inspections); Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the leased premises require a municipal establishment, occupancy, or storefront permit for a high-value resale operation and warehouse mezzanine. For a dry-goods fulfillment site, obtain the municipal fire safety clearance and confirm no industrial process authorization is necessary. If any alteration is made to the building, obtain a construction permit before work starts.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or proof of ownership
Floor plan and intended use description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal inspector requires changes, submit a revised floor plan, obtain the necessary building permit, and implement any remedial fire or structural measures before receiving final occupancy clearance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 4791 retail activity; municipal authority with general commercial permit power: Ville de Montréal, Service des permis et inspections, or equivalent local municipality
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No province-wide statutory operating license for online second-hand luxury resale; local municipal commercial permit may be required for the physical establishment

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full environmental impact assessment; dry-goods retail and warehousing are not listed under section 22 of the Environment Quality Act as contaminating activities
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC-emitting operations; sanitary wastewater must comply with municipal sewer bylaws; packaging waste and e-waste must be recovered under Quebec's residual materials management regulation; use of refrigerants, if any, must meet the HFC/CFC ban thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Municipal fire safety certification under the Fire Safety Act, including fire extinguisher placement, exit signage, and emergency lighting; CNESST workplace health and safety registration for employees; structural load verification for mezzanine pallet racks and shelving; electrical installation conformity where new fixtures are introduced.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — GST/HST Program, Business Registration On-Line service, and My Business Account portal for federal tax accounts; Revenu Québec — clicSÉQUR Affaires portal and Service québécois d'imposition for Quebec Sales Tax (QST) and provincial corporate tax administration
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident entity carrying on business in Canada must obtain a federal GST/HST account by filing Form RC1 (Request for GST/HST Registration) with the CRA, filed directly through My Business Account or the Business Registration On-Line service. Revenu Québec requires separate QST registration via clicSÉQUR Affaires (Form LM-1), conditioned on the non-resident maintaining a physical establishment in Québec or appointing a mandatary/representative resident in Québec for service of process. The federal Business Number (BN) serves as the primary TIN; the QST account is a distinct 14-digit identifier. For online consignment and secondhand luxury resale, foreign consignors using a Canadian fulfilment centre are deemed to make taxable supplies in Canada and must register once the CAD 30,000 threshold is exceeded, even absent local incorporation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a Business Corporation incorporated federally under the Canada Business Corporations Act or provincially under the Québec Business Corporations Act is a taxpayer separate from its shareholders, subject to Part I federal corporate income tax and the Québec Taxation Act corporate tax regime; no flow-through transparency for corporations; Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs) qualify for the reduced federal and Québec small business deduction rates on active business income, while the online resale platform revenue is characterized as active business income if no foreign-controlled specified services exception applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a US-style 'check-the-box' classification regime. Available statutory elections include: (i) GST/HST closely related corporation election under section 156 of the Excise Tax Act, and its QST mirror under the Québec Taxation Act, treating otherwise taxable intra-group supplies as made for nil consideration; (ii) section 216 Income Tax Act election for non-residents disposing of Canadian real property to file on a net basis; (iii) sections 73 and 85 rollover elections permitting tax-deferred transfer of vintage luxury inventory and platform goodwill into the Canadian corporation; (iv) hybrid mismatch election mechanics under Part VI.1 of the Income Tax Act (sections 18.2 and 212.3) requiring prescribed return disclosures to coordinate Canadian recharacterization of hybrid instruments or disregarded branches in cross-border resale structures; and (v) the section 156.1 GST/HST joint venture election for co-venturers operating an online marketplace.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax at 5% federal rate) plus QST (Quebec Sales Tax at 9.5% computed on the GST-inclusive price), together yielding a combined effective Quebec VAT-type burden of 14.975% applicable to taxable supplies in Quebec; resale of used luxury goods is subject to the normal GST/QST regime without margin-scheme relief.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — the CRA small-supplier threshold for GST/HST is CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies in a single calendar quarter or cumulatively over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; Revenu Québec applies the identical CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold for QST registration; non-resident online sellers exceeding this threshold through Quebec-destined sales must register and collect both taxes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not currently impose mandatory real-time fiscal electronic clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction controls for B2B/B2C invoicing. The CRA is progressively adopting the Pan-Canadian Peppol-based e-invoicing interoperability framework on a voluntary basis, and Revenu Québec is evaluating a provincial e-reporting mandate. Registrants must nevertheless issue invoices containing prescribed information (federal BN and QST registration number, tax amounts, vendor/purchaser identification), maintain electronic books and records accessible in Canada in ERP/API-ready format, and be prepared for CRA and Revenu Québec e-audit data extraction under electronic records audit protocols.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of secondhand luxury goods exported by the vendor qualify for GST/HST zero-rating under section 1 of Part V, Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act (supply of property exported in compliance with prescribed conditions) and for QST zero-rating under section 1 of Schedule III to the Regulation respecting the Québec Sales Tax, where the vendor causes the goods to be exported promptly after the sale in accordance with ordinary commercial practice, transfers continuous possession and ownership to a non-resident purchaser outside Canada, and retains documentary proof of export, including where export occurs via a third-party freight forwarder or fulfilment-centre bridge warehouse. Online consignment intermediation services supplied to non-resident consignors may also qualify for zero-rating as services to a non-resident under section 7 of Part V, Schedule VI, provided the services are not received in Canada. Proceeds from export sales are expected to be repatriated to Canada within the administrative documentary benchmark of 180 days from the date of shipment to affirm bona fide export intent.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A or electronic export reporting through the Canadian Export Reporting System / CBSA A8.1 requiring an approved carrier or freight forwarder to report the export entry)
Commercial invoice and fully executed sales or consignment contract evidencing transfer of ownership and risk to the non-resident purchaser or consignee
Transport documentation — Bill of Lading, airway bill, courier shipment manifest, or freight forwarder certificate showing physical departure of the goods from Canada and delivery outside Canada

Proof of foreign currency payment settled into a Canadian financial institution, comprising SWIFT MT103, Inward Remittance Certificate, or payment-rail settlement report from Stripe or Escrow-Pay custodial accounts

Foreign exchange contract, payment retention records, and ledger extracts demonstrating that export proceeds are received within the contractual and documentary deadlines and are fully declared for Canadian income tax and GST/HST/QST purposes
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec subject export zero-rating claims to enhanced audit scrutiny: a registrant must produce the complete export documentation bundle on demand within a 30-day statutory books-and-records request window, and any failure to substantiate zero-rating triggers reassessment of the supply at the combined 14.975% GST/QST rate with reversal of related input tax credits, statutory interest computed from the original filing due date, and penalties under section 285 of the Excise Tax Act — the greater of CAD 100 and 25% of the net tax attributed to the misstatement, increasing to 50% where the misstatement was made knowingly or through gross negligence. Knowingly creating false export documentation or fraudulently claiming export zero-rating can additionally attract criminal prosecution under section 327 of the Excise Tax Act with fines up to CAD 50,000 and imprisonment, as well as full retrospective clawback of input tax credits previously claimed on consigned vintage luxury inventory and denial of future zero-rating status.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); foreign exchange and monetary policy administered jointly with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential regulation; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for AML/CTF enforcement; Autorite des marches financiers (AMF) as the Quebec provincial securities and financial-services conduct regulator.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both current and capital account under IMF Article VIII. Canada maintains no exchange-control legislation, no surrender requirements, and no pre-approval gateways for foreign-currency purchases or cross-border remittances. The Canadian dollar floats freely. Profit remittance hurdles are exclusively tax-driven: non-resident shareholders are subject to Part XIII withholding tax at the 25% statutory default, generally treaty-reduced to 5%-15% on dividends, interest, and royalties; Form NR4 filing and bank-level sanctions/AML screening apply. A functional-currency election under section 261 of the Income Tax Act is available to keep the corporate books in USD, minimizing recurring CAD-conversion friction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Canada imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no obligation to surrender export receipts. Vintage-luxury resale revenues may be retained in USD, EUR, or CAD in any domestic or foreign account. FX gains and losses on export proceeds are ordinary income or ordinary expense for Canadian tax purposes, recorded at the Bank of Canada daily exchange rate and reported on the T2 corporation return.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account plus non-resident-friendly USD Foreign Currency Account
Operational Account with Canada-U.S. cross-border desk via BMO Harris Bank NA
Operational Account staggered with Business USD Account; Quebec-headquartered with AMF familiarity
Operational Account with integrated cross-border wire centre
Business Operating Account via cooperative credit union; regulated by AMF

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM with strict legal constraints. FINTRAC-registered money service businesses such as Wise Business, Payoneer, and Stripe Treasury are permissible for transaction settlement, multi-currency receiving, and low-value disbursement, but they are not Schedule I chartered banks and cannot lawfully maintain a regulated capital escrow account for a Canadian corporation. Offshore EMIs lacking Canadian MSB registration cannot hold settlement accounts for a Quebec entity and expose the company to uninsured, non-compliant treasury risk. EscrowPay is viable as an escrow technology rail only when structured as a trust/escrow arrangement with a chartered bank as custodian; funds held solely with the fintech are not CDIC-insured. Recommended architecture: Stripe as card-acquiring rail, EscrowPay as escrow settlement engine, and a Schedule I bank as the sole liquidity and final-disbursement treasury account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted for Canadian-resident directors who complete FINTRAC-compliant video identity verification at all Tier 1 banks. Non-resident directors, US beneficial owners, or any file triggering enhanced due diligence — consignment payouts to third-party sellers, prior use of an offshore EMI, or high-volume cross-border activity — generally require physical attendance at a domestic branch or a notarized identity interview via the bank's Canada-U.S. desk (BMO and National Bank offer remote notarization). Physical presence becomes effectively mandatory where a director or beneficial owner appears on PEP, sanctions, or adverse-media watchlists. Minimum KYC package: certificate and articles of incorporation, registered office address, completed Individual Control Register declaration, business plan, evidence of e-commerce platform contracts, and the bank's enhanced-due-diligence questionnaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value consignment payouts to unverified third-party luxury sellers with rapid EFT dispersal of sales proceeds, creating invoice-displacement and money-laundering red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed consignment agreements per seller, seller KYC files with government-issued ID, third-party authentication certificates for sold items (Entrupy, RealAuthentication, or accredited appraisers), acquisition and provenance invoices, platform listing history, quarterly CPA-reviewed payout register, and sub-ledger reconciliation to Stripe and EscrowPay settlements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border inbound wires from US or offshore personal accounts referencing investor capital without supporting corporate records, triggering reverse-source-of-funds concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share-subscription agreement or executed shareholder loan agreement, board resolution authorizing the injection, updated shareholder register and beneficial-ownership schedule, source-of-wealth questionnaire, bank reference letter from the remitting institution, and a tax memorandum confirming Part XIII withholding treatment on any deemed dividend component.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Escrow-float mismatch: large inbound funds parked for over 30 days without matching inventory, suggesting trade-based money laundering or sanctions evasion
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EscrowPay escrow agreement with explicit release conditions, escrow instructions and funds-flow diagram, inventory aging report matched to active listings, platform sales-data export, CFO attestation memorandum, and a semi-annual update of the bank's medium-risk enhanced customer risk assessment.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (1) Originate a SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder or intercompany account to the Quebec corporation's Schedule I bank account; (2) Populate field 70 with a transparent reference: CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION [ENTITY NAME] [AGREEMENT DATE] or DIRECTOR LOAN [ENTITY NAME] for debt injections; (3) Execute and archive the share-subscription agreement or loan agreement, board resolution, and updated corporate register; (4) Cash-equivalent deposits above CAD 10,000 require the bank's large-cash or large-EFT reporting form and FINTRAC reporting as applicable; (5) Any single credit above CAD 100,000 automatically triggers source-of-funds verification — respond with the full transaction dossier within three business days to prevent account hold. No prior FX approval, conversion mandate, or government fee applies to capital inflows into a Canadian entity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Preferred clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for international seller and supplier settlements, with a clean field-70 reference such as CONSIGNMENT SETTLEMENT INVOICE [INV-2024-XXXX]; (ii) Commercial Letter of Credit via SWIFT MT700 where a single supplier lot exceeds CAD 250,000 and requires documentary title transfer; (iii) Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) or the Real-Time Rail for domestic payouts to Canadian consignors, providing immediate finality; (iv) automated escrow release through EscrowPay API, funded from the corporate treasury account, to preserve the audit trail and mitigate chargeback exposure. Each payout must be mapped to the escrow settlement schedule and recorded in the accounting sub-ledger with matching entries for inventory and consignment liability.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright FX forward contracts with a Schedule I bank or an OSFI-regulated derivatives dealer, tenors up to 24 months, covering CAD/USD and CAD/EUR exposure on projected sales receipts
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on a limited best-efforts basis for exotic settlement currencies; permissible under Canadian law but not required for the CAD/USD/EUR corridor
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD floating versus fixed) with qualifying counterparties under an executed ISDA with CSA, where treasury exposure exceeds CAD 5 million annually
Vanilla FX options (put/call) purchased from a regulated Canadian dealer to cap adverse USD/CAD movement on USD-denominated consignment receivables
FX collars and out-of-the-money knockout forwards as customized OTC structures, documented under the master agreement with the treasury bank

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of incorporation or the previous annual return filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of $100 per day of default; repeated non-filing may trigger administrative dissolution

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit required if the corporation is a distributing corporation or has more than 50 shareholders (excluding directors and employees)

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Directors annually confirm corporate information including directors and officers through the annual return filing; beneficial ownership register maintained internally and updated upon share transfers

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal general corporate income tax rate: 15%. Quebec general corporate income tax rate: 11.5%. Combined general rate: 26.5%. A qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporation may generally access a federal small-business rate of 9% and a Quebec rate of approximately 3.2%, producing a combined rate of approximately 12.2% on eligible active business income within the applicable business limit, generally CAD 500,000 subject to federal and Quebec rules.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general corporate tax holiday applies to an ordinary luxury-resale corporation. Available incentives may include the federal and Quebec small-business deductions for qualifying CCPCs, accelerated capital cost allowance under applicable federal rules, Quebec investment and regional incentives where eligibility conditions are satisfied, and refundable or non-refundable research and development credits where qualifying activities exist. Inventory purchases and ordinary resale costs are generally deductible only when properly matched under inventory rules. The general Quebec sales tax and federal GST/HST regimes are separate from corporate income tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, including Schedule 1 and applicable schedules, filed electronically through CRA Corporation Internet Filing or an authorized tax software product. Quebec CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return is filed electronically through Revenu Quebec's online services. GST/HST and QST returns are separate filings through CRA and Revenu Quebec portals.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The federal T2 and Quebec CO-17 are generally due within six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end. Any balance is generally due two months after year-end; a qualifying CCPC meeting the statutory conditions generally receives a three-month balance-payment period. Instalments may be required monthly or quarterly. A corporation carrying on business in Quebec generally must file both federal and Quebec corporate returns.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, business number, corporation type, jurisdiction of incorporation, fiscal period, address, principal business activity and contact information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada must report its Canadian permanent-establishment activities, use its CRA business number, identify its jurisdiction of residence and disclose relevant non-resident status. A corporation resident in Canada is generally subject to Canadian tax on worldwide income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ownership, control, associated corporations and CCPC status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose foreign ownership, associated corporations and control relationships. Do not claim CCPC treatment unless the statutory Canadian-control requirements are satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting income to income for tax purposes, including non-deductible expenses, inventory adjustments, depreciation, reserves and other tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude accounting items not deductible under Canadian law and separately identify expenses allocated to Canadian operations. Maintain support for inventory valuation, consignment commissions, returns, chargebacks, shipping and payment-processing costs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital cost allowance and shareholder information where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim capital cost allowance only for qualifying depreciable property used to earn Canadian income. Report foreign shareholders and ownership information as required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income, federal tax calculation, small-business deduction, general rate reduction and other federal rate components.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the general rate unless the corporation demonstrably qualifies for the CCPC small-business deduction or another specific regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 23 or applicable dividend schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividends, refundable tax, investment income and corporate tax integration items where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify dividends paid to non-residents and reconcile them to T5 information slips, withholding remittances and treaty claims.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transactions with non-arm's-length non-residents and related-party reporting.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File Form T106 for reportable transactions with non-arm's-length non-residents when the applicable reporting conditions are met, including the aggregate CAD 1 million threshold rules. Reconcile related-party purchases, royalties, management fees, loans, commissions and inventory transfers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 24 and foreign reporting schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information relating to tax treaty positions, foreign affiliates, foreign property and other international tax matters where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the applicable schedule for foreign affiliates or specified foreign property. Do not claim treaty relief without documenting residence, beneficial ownership, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose requirements where relevant.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec corporation identification, fiscal period, Quebec establishment information, taxable income and Quebec income tax calculation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Quebec income attributable to a Quebec establishment. A non-resident corporation must determine whether it carries on business in Quebec and whether a Quebec permanent establishment or allocation requirement exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec reconciliation, capital cost allowance, associated corporations, business limit and applicable Quebec deductions or credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Quebec adjustments separately from federal adjustments and maintain consistent allocation of inventory, fulfillment, platform, employee and head-office costs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: GST/HST return and QST return, including taxable sales, tax collected, input tax credits or input tax refunds and net remittance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Register where required, determine place-of-supply and platform-facilitator rules, and distinguish taxable sales from exempt or zero-rated transactions. Luxury goods resales are generally taxable unless a specific rule applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T4, T4A, T5 and RL-1/RL-3 information returns
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Payroll, commissions, investment income, dividends and other reportable payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Issue slips for Canadian recipients and report non-resident dividends, interest, royalties or other amounts subject to Part XIII withholding using the applicable information returns.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Federal late-filing penalty is generally 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% of the unpaid balance for each complete month late, generally capped at 12%; higher repeated-failure penalties may apply. Quebec generally applies comparable late-filing penalties, including an initial percentage and monthly additions, subject to statutory caps. Interest accrues on unpaid tax, instalments, penalties and certain remittances at prescribed rates, compounded daily. Gross-negligence, false-statement and tax-evasion penalties can substantially exceed ordinary late-filing penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form T106 Information Return of Non-Arm's Length Transactions with Non-Residents, filed electronically with the federal T2 return or through CRA-authorized electronic filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally due by the corporation's T2 filing deadline for the relevant fiscal period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Canadian reporting corporation and fiscal-period information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the Canadian corporation and provide the applicable reporting period and business number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident related party, country of residence, relationship and arm's-length status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify every relevant foreign related party and accurately describe ownership, control and relationship status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transaction category, gross amounts, currency, income or expense classification and reporting threshold information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report purchases and sales of inventory, services, royalties, interest, commissions, loans and other transactions on a gross basis where required; retain conversion methodology and transfer-pricing support.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Penalties apply for late, incomplete or inaccurate T106 filing and may be assessed per form or per failure. Repeated or deliberate non-compliance can support transfer-pricing penalties and broader reassessment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The domestic Canadian Part XIII withholding rate on dividends paid or credited to a non-resident is 25%. A treaty commonly reduces the rate to 15% for portfolio dividends and to 5% where the treaty ownership and corporate-recipient conditions are satisfied; the precise rate depends on the applicable treaty, ownership percentage, voting rights, beneficial ownership and anti-abuse provisions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain and retain a valid certificate of residence or equivalent documentary evidence, establish beneficial ownership and treaty eligibility, review limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose provisions where applicable, and obtain Form NR301, NR302 or NR303 when relevant to the recipient's status. The Canadian payer must apply the correct rate, remit withholding to CRA generally by the 15th day of the following month, file the applicable T4A-NR or NR4 information return, and issue the recipient slip. Where excessive withholding occurred, the non-resident generally seeks a refund from CRA using the applicable procedure. Treaty relief is not automatic merely because the recipient is incorporated in a treaty country.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The domestic Part XIII rate is generally 25% on royalties and interest paid to non-residents, subject to statutory exceptions and treaty reductions. Many Canadian treaties reduce interest withholding to 10%, and some eliminate withholding on qualifying arm's-length interest or particular debt instruments. Royalties commonly receive treaty rates of 10% or 15%, while some copyright, software, industrial, scientific or literary royalty categories may receive a lower or zero rate depending on the treaty definition. Payments must be classified by legal substance; service fees, software access, platform fees, financing charges and trademark or copyright royalties can have different outcomes.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Canada does not impose a single universal bright-line threshold for maintaining contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation. Form T106 reporting generally applies under the applicable CAD 1 million aggregate transaction threshold rules. A Canadian taxpayer must maintain contemporaneous documentation supporting arm's-length pricing and provide it to CRA on request. Canadian entities in an MNE group with consolidated revenue of at least CAD 1 billion may have Country-by-Country reporting obligations and may be required to provide a Master File or equivalent information under the applicable international reporting framework. The CAD 1 million and CAD 1 billion thresholds must not be treated as a general exemption from local transfer-pricing documentation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no general standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime equivalent to the UAE or certain offshore jurisdictions. Nevertheless, CRA may challenge arrangements under the Income Tax Act transfer-pricing rules, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule, treaty anti-abuse provisions, beneficial-ownership principles, residence and central-management-and-control concepts, and the requirement that expenses be incurred to earn income. A Canadian corporation should maintain Canadian decision-making evidence, commercial rationale, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, inventory and fulfillment records, banking controls, customer and supplier contracts, and substance proportionate to its resale activities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate income-tax evasion and false reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing online sales, understating resale margins, fabricating consignment expenses, claiming personal luxury purchases as inventory, manipulating inventory counts, or knowingly submitting false T2 or CO-17 information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under the Income Tax Act may result in a fine generally ranging from 50% to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment of up to five years. Civil reassessment, arrears interest, gross-negligence penalties and unreported-income penalties may apply separately.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may face personal criminal exposure for knowing participation, authorization or acquiescence. Directors may also be assessed personally for certain corporate remittance liabilities. Travel restrictions are not an automatic tax sanction but may arise through ordinary criminal-process mechanisms, including bail or judicial orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register when required, omitting taxable marketplace sales, issuing false invoices, claiming unsupported input tax credits or input tax refunds, or treating taxable luxury-goods sales as exempt.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of unremitted GST/HST or QST, interest, civil penalties and potentially criminal prosecution. False statements and tax-evasion provisions can produce substantial fines and imprisonment under federal and Quebec legislation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly and severally liable for certain unremitted GST/HST and Quebec source or consumption taxes where statutory due-diligence defenses are unavailable. Personal liability is generally imposed by statute rather than automatic piercing of the corporate veil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Treating employees as contractors without support, failing to withhold income tax, CPP or EI, failing to remit deductions, or paying undeclared commissions to sales agents.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of unremitted deductions, employer contributions, interest and penalties; serious cases may attract criminal sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be assessed personally under the Income Tax Act for corporate source deductions if statutory conditions are met and due diligence is not established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using non-arm's-length foreign procurement, licensing, management, financing or commission arrangements without support; shifting resale profit to a related foreign entity; or failing to file T106.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may adjust income under the arm's-length principle, impose transfer-pricing penalties generally equal to 10% of the adjustment where the statutory conditions are satisfied, assess interest and apply reassessment periods or information penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors generally face corporate civil exposure rather than automatic personal transfer-pricing liability, but personal criminal exposure can arise from intentional false statements, obstruction or tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Counterfeit, stolen or illicit luxury goods
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly acquiring, consigning, importing, marketing or selling counterfeit, stolen or crime-derived handbags, watches, jewelry, apparel or other luxury goods.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Seizure, forfeiture, customs penalties, civil trademark or copyright damages, injunctions and potential Criminal Code prosecution for possession of property obtained by crime, fraud, trafficking or proceeds-of-crime offences. Penalties depend on the conduct and evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals who direct, authorize, knowingly facilitate or personally participate may be prosecuted and may face restitution, forfeiture, fines or imprisonment. Corporate limited liability does not protect participants in criminal conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting suspicious third-party payments, structuring cash or virtual-asset transactions, failing to identify clients, failing to retain records, failing to report suspicious transactions, or operating as a money-services business without registration where registration is required.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties may be imposed by FINTRAC, with serious violations potentially reaching CAD 100,000 for an individual and CAD 500,000 for an entity per violation under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act framework. Criminal money-laundering offences can result in significant fines and imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Compliance officers, directors and responsible persons may face personal administrative or criminal exposure where they participated in, directed, consented to or deliberately ignored the violation. A shell company is not unlawful per se, but concealment of beneficial ownership or use for laundering or evasion is a critical red flag.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining nominee arrangements, concealing controlling persons, filing inaccurate beneficial-ownership information, or using layered entities to obscure ownership, related-party transactions or proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate-law penalties, tax reassessment, denial of treaty benefits, enhanced compliance review and potential criminal or proceeds-of-crime charges may apply depending on the conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may face statutory penalties and criminal liability for knowingly false corporate filings or participation in concealment. Corporate veil protection does not shield fraud or deliberate statutory breaches.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, royalties or other Part XIII amounts to foreign recipients without withholding, relying on unsupported treaty rates, or failing to file NR4 information returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Canadian payer may be liable for the unwithheld amount, interest and penalties, generally without being able to recover the full liability from the foreign recipient. Treaty benefits may be denied where beneficial ownership or anti-abuse requirements fail.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal liability for statutory remittance debts in appropriate cases, particularly where they authorized payments or failed to exercise due diligence. Criminal exposure requires additional facts showing knowing or fraudulent conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Transferring inventory, cash or receivables to related parties before tax enforcement, preferring insiders, falsifying books, or stripping assets from the corporation to defeat CRA, Revenu Quebec or trade creditors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transactions may be set aside, assets recovered, directors disqualified or sued, and criminal fraud or bankruptcy offences may apply. Tax debts, penalties and interest remain enforceable against the corporation and potentially responsible persons.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil restitution, contribution claims, statutory director-liability assessments and criminal prosecution. Imprisonment is possible for fraudulent conduct; travel bans are not automatic and require a legal basis such as bail, arrest or court order.
